newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi prevented from giving speech.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi prevented from giving speech.

text.p: Burma's opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi was prevented from addressing the public on Saturday as police barred access to her home and turned away at least 250 people who had come to see her.

"The police turned away several hundred people who gathered near police checkpoints leading to Suu Kyi's University Avenue residence. There was no chaos but police firmly asked them to go away," one witness said.

Suu Kyi had said last Tuesday, when another set of checkpoints barring access to her home from September 26 were removed, that she was ready to address the public again at the weekend after failing to do so for two consecutive weeks because of the barriers.
She was not available for comment as it appeared the telephone line to her home was cut and repeated attempts to reach her failed.

Since her release last July the democracy leader has been addressing several thousand supporters every weekend from the gates of her residence. In her speeches, she has sought more democracy in Burma from the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
But the SLORC, which has labelled her weekend gatherings illegal, blocked public access to Suu Kyi's residence on Saturday with traffic and armed security police manning the checkpoints.
A government official told Reuters it was to prevent her weekend public gatherings from becoming a flashpoint for any disturbances. But he said nobody had been detained.

"The government as a preventive measure restricted traffic to the road. We also do not want the situation (public gatherings) to be exploited by anybody to disturb the peace and tranquility of the people," the official said.
He could not say when the checkpoints would be removed but residents in the area said they believed they could be lifted on Monday.

The official added that the action to bar access followed information that Suu Kyi and some officials of her National League for Democracy Party (NLD) had planned to hold a meeting in her residence on Saturday morning to discuss the re-staging of a party congress which was abandoned late last month.

An NLD member of parliament said all NLD MPs from Rangoon had been invited to attend an informal meeting in Suu Kyi's house on Saturday morning but when he came near the house he found that the road was closed.
"We are not disappointed but we don't know what we'll decide to do next," said the MP who asked for anonymity.
Access to the opposition leader's house was first barred on September 26, to stop a planned September 27-29 NLD congress.
After the congress was effectively scotched, the military removed the barriers on Tuesday.
As well as barring access to Suu Kyi's home, the SLORC also cracked down at that time on NLD party activists to thwart the congress and detained 573 NLD members and supporters.
All detainees were later released in stages.

"I don't think this time it will be necessary to detain anyone," the government official said when asked if anyone was being detained in addition to the setting up of checkpoints along University Avenue this time.
Eighteen NLD party flags remained draped over the fence of Suu Kyi's home. They were first flown in late September ahead of the failed party congress.
The official Burmese media on Saturday quoted a senior SLORC official, Secretary Two, Lieutenant-General Tin Oo as warning "some unscrupulous people" against disturbing the peace.
"It is found that some unscrupulous people are covertly perpetrating acts to undermine public security with intent to jeopardise the country's peace and tranquility," the media quoted him as saying.
He warned that "security measures will be carried out and effective action will be taken" to prevent any disturbance.
Burma's action against Suu Kyi and NLD supporters last month drew condemnation from the United States, Britain and international human rights groups.
